bounds: evidence/m3-ao-bvh-bounds.json (4619cea, before any code or run)
ci: workflow .github/workflows/ao-oracle.yml, run 39075389683 (PR #180, ubuntu-24.04, GCC); the unit guard also ran locally on MSVC with the same numbers of identical pixels

g1_unit.observed: AO from the BVH bit-identical to the scan on every covered pixel: test scene 128 x 128 (9,496 of 9,496), sphere grid 96 x 96 (5,524 of 5,524), raw-hero 64 x 40 (1,299 of 1,299).

g2_golden.observed: The BVH runs equal the committed goldens: identity matrix 11 cases and 119 files including arena_certificate.json, all identical; glTF models 10 cases, 80 files compared as the main CI does (arena certificate left out), all identical. The golden does not change.

g3_oracle.observed: BVH against the scan oracle, every file including the arena certificate: identity matrix 11 cases, 119 files; glTF 10 cases, 90 files; all identical.

g4_control.observed: The skew control (BVH query distance 1% short) breaks the unit guard on all three scenes (worst 1/32, 3/64 and 1/16 against a one-sample bound) and makes the identity matrix differ from the scan.

g5_cost.observed: computeRTAO on raw-hero 64 x 40, 16 samples: BVH 3.5 ms against scan 13,701 ms on the CI runner (about 3,900 times), 1.8 ms against 6,641 ms locally. Sphere grid: 104 ms against 8,064 ms. Test scene (14 triangles): 50 ms against 104 ms.

does_not_prove: That the AO estimate is right; anything about the GPU rtao and raster passes, which still scan every triangle per pixel.
